name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 4th European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) takes place in Vienna, Austria from 6 to 10 July 2026. It offers a one‑week program of introductory and advanced AI courses, tutorials, and tracks on the special themes of Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, targeting PhD students, young researchers, and senior scholars. The school also provides networking opportunities, a reception at Vienna City Hall, and is co‑located with the 5th ACM Europe Digital Humanism Summer School.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen conference hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries and doctoral students, offering technical presentations, hands‑on elements, and discussions on multilingual large language models and their evaluation. The program includes expert talks, a walk‑through of EuroHPC experience reports, and networking opportunities, with travel and accommodation subsidized by the OpenEuroLLM project.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: The Probabilistic AI School 2026 is a short intensive program taking place in Vilnius, Lithuania. It aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine‑learning and artificial‑intelligence topics for students, researchers and industry professionals. The school brings together enthusiasts and experts to foster collaboration and knowledge exchange in probabilistic AI.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
venue: Durham University, Durham, England, United Kingdom
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a wide range of computer‑vision topics, delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme features daily oral talks and hands‑on sessions designed for graduate students and early‑career researchers seeking advanced training and networking opportunities.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: OxML 2026 brought three advanced machine learning programmes together across online and hybrid formats, with participants learning from leading researchers and practitioners. The programmes covered practical AI model building (MLx Cases), health and biomedical AI (MLx Health & Bio), and representation learning and generative AI (MLx Representation Learning & Gen AI). The school was hosted by the Oxford Machine Learning School and provided recordings and programme materials through the Elandi learning dashboard.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers focusing on robotics, perception and learning. It covers topics such as machine learning, computer vision, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making, and combines keynote talks, industry panels, brainstorming sessions and student presentations. The school takes place at the Happy Tammsvik resort in Stockholm, offering a relaxed setting with indoor and outdoor activities to foster new collaborations.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School 2027 is a five‑day event held from 21 to 25 June 2027 in Edinburgh, Scotland. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials, industry talks and hands‑on experience with state‑of‑the‑art robotics technology, aiming to foster learning, engagement and knowledge exchange in the field of robotics. The programme is targeted at master’s‑level students and industry practitioners and includes networking opportunities, refreshments and a special dinner.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2027 Biometrics Summer School takes place in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy, hosted at the Hotel Dei Pini. It focuses on the impact of agentic AI and vision foundation models on biometrics, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, forensic and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers, forensic examiners and professionals, offering lectures by 18 international experts, hands‑on sessions, and optional videoconference participation.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems (ELSAI and AS) is announced as a dedicated event. It concentrates on exploring the ethical, legal, and societal implications of artificial intelligence and autonomous systems. Related projects from the school are made available on GitHub by the mlwinterschoolumea team.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM’27) will be held from 1–5 February 2027 in the Vercors mountains near Grenoble. It aims to bring together PhD students and early‑career researchers from fields such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing and human‑robot interaction for cross‑disciplinary exchange through lectures, hands‑on sessions and informal networking. The mountain setting also offers outdoor activities, fostering collaboration and a scientific retreat atmosphere.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 Winter School runs from 11 to 15 January in Tromsø as part of the Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference. It provides intensive lectures and training on cutting‑edge deep‑learning topics such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction and speech recognition. The programme is aimed at researchers and practitioners who wish to exchange ideas, build collaborations, and stay up‑to‑date with the latest advances in deep learning.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School is an 11‑day intensive in‑person program offering AI lectures, labs, and project work. It targets senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals, covering fundamentals to cutting‑edge topics such as geometric deep learning, generative modeling, world models, and neuro‑symbolic AI. The school aims to build AI research capacity in Nepal and the region by providing hands‑on training, networking opportunities, and exposure to state‑of‑the‑art research.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It offers a series of lectures and tutorials on advanced machine‑learning topics delivered by leading researchers from institutions such as Google DeepMind, MIT, and the University of Montenegro. The program is aimed at graduate students and early‑career researchers in the region who seek intensive training and networking opportunities.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
venue: Mediterranean Machine Learning Summer School, Barcelona, Spain
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day program in Barcelona, Spain that offers keynotes, lectures, and practical sessions on AI. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, academics and practitioners, emphasizing state‑of‑the‑art topics such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, reinforcement learning and ethics in machine learning. The school promotes diversity, networking, and collaboration through scholarships, poster sessions, and social activities.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 (AthNLP) is a week‑long program held at the NCSR Demokritos campus in Athens, Greece. It brings together experts from RC Athena, NCSR Demokritos, Athens University of Economics and Business, Heriot‑Watt University, Archimedes Unit, and ELLIS‑University of Manchester to cover recent advances in NLP. The school also supports the 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence, providing participants with additional workshops and networking opportunities.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The AI For Finance summer school is offered by Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, as part of the LMH Oxford Summer Programmes. It focuses on artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques applied to financial problems, covering topics such as robust ML, continual learning, and malicious user detection. The programme is available as a residential or online course running from 28 June to 16 July 2027 and is aimed at students and professionals interested in AI-driven finance.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive programme that offers courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management, inventive thinking and the intersection of business and technology. The programme combines online instruction with a on‑campus teaching week at LUT University’s Lappeenranta campus in August 2027 and includes workshops, group work and a social programme set in Finnish nature. It is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students from other universities as well as LUT students, providing 3 ECTS credits per course.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: The AIces 2026 International School focuses on the cognitive, ethical, and societal dimensions of artificial intelligence. It is aimed at graduate and postgraduate students as well as industry practitioners, offering parallel courses, a symposium, and open debates. The event takes place in Porto and Maia, Portugal from 30 March to 2 April 2026, with both face‑to‑face and live‑online participation and recordings available for 45 days.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition of the AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI is a five‑day immersive program held at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It offers young researchers, Ph.D. and master students, post‑docs, and industry professionals a mix of theoretical lectures, hands‑on labs, and project mentorship covering state‑of‑the‑art multimodal and generative AI techniques. The school is jointly organized by MoroccoAI, INPT, IMT Nord Europe and Soft Centre, providing networking opportunities with leading AI experts and fostering the next generation of AI leaders in Morocco.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI brings together researchers, PhD students and post‑doctoral scholars in Caen, Normandy, France. It focuses on applying deep‑learning techniques to accelerate scientific research, covering topics such as machine‑learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration of AI with physical simulations. The programme combines lectures with hands‑on Python workshops using libraries like NumPy and PyTorch, aiming to equip participants with practical skills for AI‑enhanced scientific discovery.
